source.title: Proof of a perfect platonic representation hypothesis

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Provides an analytical test of representation alignment in an idealized embedded deep linear network, using a theoretical objective and proof rather than the empirical measurements of the original PRH work. It also derives conditions under which perfect alignment fails.
record.gate_note: The paper reports mathematical results for an embedded deep linear network (EDLN), not experiments on trained vision or language models. Its cross-network theorem assumes global minima of the entropic objective; the text does not demonstrate that ordinary SGD training reaches those minima. Empirical alignment values mentioned in the discussion are attributed to other work and are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: A theoretical note on the embedded deep linear network (EDLN). It proves perfect alignment at global minima of the SGD entropic objective, independent of width, depth, initialization and input view. It then derives six conditions that break this alignment: weight decay, gradient flow, label transforms, saddles, data heterogeneity and edge of stability. It also argues the cause is parameter symmetry plus entropic forces, not capacity, simplicity or multitasking. These are analytic arguments that versions need restating, not empirical measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that the cause is parameter symmetry plus SGD's entropic force, none of the PRH paper's conjectured mechanisms (capacity, simplicity, multitasking). They link it to progressive sharpening. They note real models reach only about 0.2 CKA, so extending the theory to nonlinear models and weaker forms of the PRH is open.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical proof for an embedded deep linear network using a gradient-norm entropic objective; no empirical model-similarity experiment or scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper derives different alignment outcomes for entropic-objective minimization, weight decay, gradient flow, label transformations, heterogeneous data, saddle or local minima, and edge-of-stability conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-network layer-to-layer alignment: every pair of layers in one EDLN is perfectly aligned at entropic minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layers within a network converge to the same representation up to rotation under SGD implicit regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: In the EDLN, the force driving Platonic representations is the same one driving progressive sharpening.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation convergence co-occurs with progressive sharpening or flattening.

record.problems: The result is restricted to an idealized linear model and global-minimum conditions. The paper does not establish that SGD reaches those minima, test actual modalities or capability scaling, or empirically verify its proposed break conditions. It states that extension to nonlinear models is an open problem.
record.rows_left_out: No cited empirical findings from other papers were included as rows. The discussion's cited real-model CKA value is explicitly attributed to prior work, not measured in this study.

untested.parts: Entire version. There is no size or capability variation, and the paper says its result holds for networks of identical capacity.
Entire version. Modalities are abstracted as invertible linear input views; there are no vision or language models, captions, or performance trend.
No empirical seed experiments or feature or unit matching in trained networks. The result is analytic for EDLNs only.
Entire version. No neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Entire version. No comparison of similarity metrics, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution measurement inputs.

missing.what: Perfect alignment needs label noise independent of x and full-rank. If the prediction residual depends on x, as with generic y(x), the global minimum is not Platonic.
Mechanism argument: alignment arises from parameter symmetry plus entropic forces, not from capacity, simplicity bias or multitasking.
missing.locator: Section 6, 'Cause of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis'

record.verdict_notes: Purely analytic. Most break conditions are informal or 'hand-wavy' arguments, and the label-transform result is stated as not empirically confirmed. The experimental confirmation in deep linear nets and the 0.2 CKA figure are cited from other work. Some rows carry states describing the absence of alignment; for V7 that absence is the version's predicted effect, so the V7 verdicts read them that way.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no empirical nonlinear-model test or demonstration that alignment rises as models improve. The theorem concerns EDLNs at global minima of the entropic objective.

Paired views are represented by invertible linear input transformations, not actual vision and language models or image-caption inputs. No change in alignment with increasing model performance is tested.
No seed-wise training experiment or measurement of shared features or subspaces across independently initialized trained networks.
No empirical linear mapping, layer stitching, relative-representation method, or unpaired-data mapping is tested.
No interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.

The paper does not compare similarity metrics or metric settings, such as neighbour counts, or report out-of-distribution measurements. It gives theoretical results about input transformations, label transformations, and data heterogeneity.

No empirical plateau or partial-alignment trajectory is measured. The paper's evidence is theoretical and conditional on the EDLN setting; empirical CKA values in the discussion are cited from prior work.
